title: The Private Workers Can't Pull Updates
symptom: Security flagged worker-1 as missing a month of patches. Its nightly patch job has failed every night, with an error nobody has read. The website is fine, and someone swears there's a NAT gateway 'costing us money every month', so outbound access should work.

goals.description: worker-1 can reach package repositories on the internet (443)

evidence.description: the failure, seen from the worker itself
that the NAT gateway really exists and is healthy
where the private subnet's traffic actually goes

question.prompt: Why can't worker-1 reach the internet?
options: worker-1 needs a public IP address
The private subnet's route table has no 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing at the NAT gateway. The NAT exists, but nothing sends traffic to it
SSM Session Manager is blocking outbound traffic

debrief: A NAT gateway doesn't do anything by itself; a route has to send traffic to it. The private route table only had the 'local' route, so worker-1 could talk inside the VPC and nowhere else, while the team paid for an idle NAT. Two things worth noticing. First, you could still get a shell on a box with no internet access: SSM Session Manager works here because the VPC has interface endpoints for ssm, ssmmessages and ec2messages ('aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints'). Without those endpoints, SSM would have failed too and you'd have been locked out, which is why the endpoints are worth having. Second, the fix was a route, not a public IP. Giving a private worker a public IP to 'fix' its updates would expose it to the internet and bypass the design. For AWS package repos specifically, an S3 gateway endpoint can avoid NAT charges entirely.
